title: pvVisItLAMMPSDumpReader
body:
## pvVisItLAMMPSDumpReader

Reads LAMMPS molecular-dynamics dump files (.dump, text with ITEM: sections) in which one file holds many time steps: each step becomes a time of a point mesh of atoms with the dumped per-atom columns as point arrays. ParaView 5.13.3 has no native LAMMPS dump reader; pvVisItLAMMPSStructureReader reads LAMMPS structure files instead. One file supplies every time step the format stores.

Common mistakes and assumptions:

- The first mesh is the box "unitCell", so without Meshes = ["mesh"] the atoms are not read.
- Atom ids and types are numbers, not element names; map them to species yourself.
- Name the arrays you need in PointArrays and CellArrays: the VisIt bridge starts with every variable unselected, so omitting them normally gives geometry without fields.
- Schemaxis generates this binding from ParaView's catalogue and has not run a native acceptance check for this reader; check meshes, arrays and times on your own data.

Native constructor: `VisItLAMMPSDumpReader`. Identity: `sources/VisItLAMMPSDumpReader`. Role: `pipeline`. Output kinds: `["data"]`.

### Inputs

No connected inputs (source/resource).


### Options

| Key | Meaning / native assignment | Type and constraints | Default / required | Example value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `CellArrays` | Names of the zone-centred (cell) variables to read from LAMMPS dump data; each becomes a cell-data array on every selected mesh that defines it. Vector variables arrive as one multi-component array, while VisIt expressions and tensor, label, species and array variables are not converted by the bridge. The LAMMPS dump plugin declares its variables node-centred, so this list normally stays empty. | `{"items":{"type":"string"},"type":"array"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `["REPLACE_WITH_VALUE"]` |
| `FileName` | Path of the single LAMMPS dump file to read (.dump); the reader takes every time step the format stores from it. Use an absolute path; relative paths are not resolved against the JSON file's folder (Studio uses the directory it was launched from). Fixed at construction; cannot vary per visit. | `{"minLength":1,"type":"string"}` | `required` | `"REPLACE_WITH_VALUE"` |
| `Materials` | Names of materials to convert into volume-fraction cell arrays. For each selected material the bridge adds a float cell array named after it: 1 in cells made only of that material, its volume fraction in mixed cells and -1 where it is absent. The LAMMPS dump plugin defines no materials, so this list has nothing to select. | `{"items":{"type":"string"},"type":"array"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `["REPLACE_WITH_VALUE"]` |
| `Meshes` | Names of the LAMMPS dump meshes to read. Each selected mesh becomes one named block of the multiblock output and unlisted meshes are skipped. The LAMMPS dump plugin reports the simulation box "unitCell" first and the point mesh of atoms "mesh" second, so by default only the box is read. | `{"items":{"type":"string"},"type":"array"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `["REPLACE_WITH_VALUE"]` |
| `PointArrays` | Names of the node-centred (point) variables to read from LAMMPS dump data; each becomes a point-data array on every selected mesh that defines it. Vector variables arrive as one multi-component array, while VisIt expressions and tensor, label, species and array variables are not converted by the bridge. For LAMMPS dump data these are node-centred per-atom columns such as "id", "species" and the extra columns of the dump. | `{"items":{"type":"string"},"type":"array"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `["REPLACE_WITH_VALUE"]` |

Execution contract:

```json
{
  "mode": "serial",
  "performance": "unknown"
}
```

Coverage and unbound native properties:

```json
{
  "defaults": "native defaults for omitted options",
  "gaps": {},
  "origin": "generated",
  "output": "native inspection required; explicit output-port selection available",
  "outputPorts": null,
  "qualification": "not-run"
}
```

### Syntax example

Place in `nodes`. Data outputs may be selected by a scene; resource outputs must be connected to a compatible consumer.

```json
{
  "id": "result",
  "filter": "pvVisItLAMMPSDumpReader",
  "options": {
    "FileName": "REPLACE_WITH_VALUE"
  }
}
```
